PullRequest.Title: Fix customization marketplace sign-in
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

- explicitly bind the current GitHub credential to the hidden customization policy session through the SDK's supported `session.gitHubAuth.setCredentials` API
- pass the canonical configured GitHub host URL so GitHub Enterprise credentials and Copilot-user metadata use the correct authority
- preserve signed-out behavior, report degraded account metadata, and clean up the partially created hidden session when credential binding fails
- remove the superseded protected-resource fallback; no SDK/runtime change or `runtimeOverride` is used

The hidden session could report authenticated metadata while the SDK catalog auth manager still had no selected session credential. Catalog search therefore returned `authentication-required / no-credential`, and the recovery button appeared inert. Installing the session-owned credential after session creation selects it for SDK catalog operations.

## Validation

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts` — passed (134 tests)
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotSessionLauncher.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts` — passed
- `git diff --check` — passed
- real Code OSS UI scenario on macOS arm64, Dev 1.143.0 — passed against `/Users/paulwang/Desktop/shared/code/vscode-sdk-skill-install` using the normal signed-in profile, checked-in SDK/runtime, no injected token, no synthetic response, and no runtime override. Searching `figma` returned six `Skill · GitHub Feed` results with no Sign In prompt.

## How to Test

1. Sign in to Copilot in Code OSS.
2. Select the Copilot harness and open Agent Customizations.
3. Open Browse and search for `figma`.
4. Verify GitHub Feed skill results appear and no marketplace Sign In prompt is shown.

Scenarios.Scenario: Search the customization marketplace from an unmaterialized/no-chat session while signed in
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The request gets/starts the Copilot client, creates or reuses a hidden policy session, and then performs catalog.search. On a cold hidden session, mcp.discover and createSession were already serial prerequisites; the diff adds an awaited session.rpc.gitHubAuth.setCredentials call before catalog.search can begin. On a warm hidden session this setup is skipped.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ensure/start the Copilot SDK runtime client when it is not already running
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per cold client lifecycle, independent of result count
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same client startup was already required.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before hidden-session creation and catalog search

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover MCP servers and create the hidden SDK session
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One discover RPC and one session creation per cold hidden policy session
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Both boundaries already ran before each hidden-session creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install the current GitHub credential into the hidden session via gitHubAuth.setCredentials
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per signed-in hidden-session creation after coalescing; zero while signed out
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No explicit credential-binding RPC ran, leaving catalog authentication unselected for this session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: New awaited prerequisite before the first catalog operation; any internal metadata/network resolution is not independently established by repository code

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per effective catalog page, with existing pagination behavior
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same catalog search occurred, but could return authentication-required because the hidden session lacked a selected credential.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Returns marketplace results after policy-session setup

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The added work scales with hidden-policy-session creation, not catalog result count or search count. Concurrent cold requests share policySessionCreation, and subsequent requests reuse one session until its 10-minute idle release or an auth/client lifecycle change.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Hidden session creation is promise-coalesced globally in CopilotCustomizationInstallations. The added credential RPC executes once for that shared creation; it does not fan out by query, result, MCP server, or candidate.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold: one hidden session is created and credential-bound. Warm: the cached session is touched and reused, so no additional setCredentials call. The session is invalidated on auth/client changes and expires after ten minutes idle; failed creation is not cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the added awaited IPC and its once-per-cold-session reachability; low confidence that it adds a separate network request.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The latency of setCredentials and whether its implementation performs a remote metadata lookup are not visible in this repository. The confirmed incremental cost is one coalesced IPC round trip on cold signed-in policy-session creation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The constant, coalesced credential-binding RPC is the behavior required to make the subsequent authenticated catalog operation work, is skipped on warm reuse, and has no collection fan-out or unbounded lifecycle. No bounded alternative preserving the required ordering is evidenced.

Scenarios.Scenario: List, recover, install, or uninstall customizations without a visible Copilot chat session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: These operations obtain the same hidden policy session before issuing their existing SDK installation RPCs. The diff adds the same credential-binding RPC only when that shared hidden session is cold; list/recover then issue their existing skill and MCP RPCs in parallel, while prepare/apply operations retain their existing sequencing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover MCP configuration, create the hidden session, and bind credentials
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sequence per cold hidden session; only the final credential-binding RPC is new
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Discovery and creation occurred, but explicit credential binding did not.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before installation APIs receive the policySessionId

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke SDK skill/MCP list, recovery, planning, or apply APIs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: List/recover use two grouped calls; other operations use their existing bounded operation sequence
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same operation calls and concurrency were present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Performs the requested management operation after session setup

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: Transitive SDK skill/MCP installation APIs called by CopilotCustomizationInstallations
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: SDK customization installation planning/apply may inspect or modify installation files
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Depends on the selected single operation and its reviewed file set, not changed by this diff
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Installation filesystem work was already performed by the same SDK APIs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing operation-specific work after policy setup

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The added cost is one per hidden-session lifecycle regardless of installation count, candidate count, or the two skill/MCP service branches.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cold creation is coalesced across concurrent operations. Existing list/recover skill and MCP calls use Promise.all after the one shared session is ready; credential setup itself is serialized once before them.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: All operation types share the same positive cached policy session and ten-minute idle timer. Failed creation clears policySessionCreation and does not pin a negative result.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in coalescing, lifecycle, and ordering from the service implementation and tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: SDK-internal duration is not available, but the new cardinality is definitively one credential RPC per shared session rather than per installation or per file.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change adds no fan-out by installation/file count and does not reduce existing parallelism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a hidden policy session while signed out or while credential binding fails
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Signed out, the token guard skips the new RPC and returns the session as before. With a token and a binding failure, the new path awaits disconnect and then deleteSession before surfacing the error.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero if tokenless; one for a signed-in creation attempt
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No binding attempt or binding-failure path existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Determines whether the hidden session can be returned

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Disconnect and delete the partially created hidden session after binding failure
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one disconnect plus one delete per failed coalesced creation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This failure mode did not exist because credential binding was not attempted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Delays error propagation by bounded cleanup but releases the runtime/session resources

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Zero added boundary calls for signed-out creation. Failure cleanup is bounded to one disconnect and one delete for the single partially created session per failed, coalesced creation attempt.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Creation remains coalesced. Failure cleanup is intentionally sequential for one session; concurrent callers observe the same creation rejection rather than each running cleanup.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A failed creation is removed from policySessionCreation and the session ID set; no failed session is cached. A later user operation may retry with a new session, but there is no automatic retry loop in the changed path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the token guard, bounded cleanup, and failed-creation cache clearing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Individual cleanup latency is unknown; there is no evidence of automatic retry frequency or unbounded failure churn.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Signed-out behavior adds no work, and the failure-only cleanup trades bounded error-path latency for avoiding retained session resources.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all three changed files and traced the hidden customization policy session through marketplace search, installation management, authentication lifecycle, SDK IPC, subprocess startup, catalog/network work, filesystem effects, coalescing, cache expiry, and failure cleanup. The only new steady-state performance mechanism is one awaited credential-binding IPC per cold signed-in hidden session; it is coalesced, reused for ten minutes, required before authenticated catalog use, and does not scale with queries, results, installations, or files. No high-confidence actionable performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
